scenarios.journey: First launch in disposable user/app state
scenarios.captureRequirements: Welcome/setup, permissions, download/provision progress, cancel/resume if offered, actual ready state. Preserve initial evidence before changing defaults.
Launch/reopen, partial readiness, resource appearance, CLI readiness, persistent markers.

scenarios.journey: Close UI while a fixture runs
scenarios.captureRequirements: Closure/reopen, backend and HTTP continuity, resource identity/start time.
Prompt, progress, client failure, recovery and data; distinguish each lifecycle scope.
Containers/images/volumes/networks/builds/cluster/machines, menus, tabs, search/no-match, selection, keyboard and minimum-size layout.
Create entry if any; name/ports/mounts/command controls; start/stop/restart/pause/resume availability and actual target state.
Status and exit/health details, errors and offered next actions; do not misclassify application exit as engine loss.
Actions/context menu/shortcut confirmations; mixed states, per-item partial results and retained volumes.

scenarios.journey: Two Compose stacks with distinct names
scenarios.captureRequirements: Group hierarchy, project versus service selection, service names, returned metadata, source-file entry points.
Up/start/stop/restart/down controls, aggregate output, readiness/partial failures and remaining resources.
How configuration is discovered/reused, working directory, active profiles, services, reviewed source and repeat actions.
Actual menus and error/deletion behavior; recovery when source files are restored or relocated.
Missing image/unavailable port, failure attribution, cancel/retry and exact containers/networks/volume results.
Follow/history, search/highlight/context/filter, wrap, service selection, copy/export and bounded-history behavior.
Open/reopen, input/resize/Ctrl+C/exit/disconnect, focus and editing shortcuts; missing shell and stopped target.
Entry, initial tools, target identity/privileges, install-tool flow if available, cancellation, target exit and package/data preservation.
Idle/load display, units, history, paused/stopped target and read failure; avoid latency conclusions from remote desktop.
Progress/cancel, absent reference, authentication failure, multiple tags, in-use deletion and confirmations.
Submit entry, progress, cancel, retained history/steps/logs, local image use and cleanup.
Login entry if present, failed auth, retry/forget; only disposable credentials, no secret screenshots.
Folder action, Finder/editor entry, running/stopped container, directory/text/binary/large/Unicode files, path continuity.
Permission/read-only refusal, editor save/reload, external replacement/concurrent writer and actual filesystem results.
Read-only browsing, image/tag replacement, permissions and denied write; note image-store limitations.
Attached/unattached volume entry, native editing, owner/mode/symlinks, actual data and helper/resource side effects.
Create/attach/inspect/remove, in-use refusal, persistence across container recreation; exact delete consequences.
Inventory actual offered capabilities; selected cleanup/refusal, consistency warnings, cancel and preservation of unselected data. Absence is not backup success.
Default names, open/copy/index entry, browser and CLI reachability; creation/recreation/stop/removal and stale links.
Detection and explicit override, ambiguous listeners, name collisions, non-HTTP access and unavailable target.
Setup prompt, denial/cancel, retry, certificate properties and actually trusted response. Keep clean initial trust state.
Browser, host CLI, supported containers and Linux machine; opt-out, read-only/missing CA store, restart and trust removal.
Published-port conflict, host access, exposure scope and any configurable network boundary; compare routing with actual responses.
Observe configuration/status and bounded failure/recovery only with independent access restoration. If unsafe or unsupported, record blocked; never sever the only remote route.
Setup/version/readiness, cancellation if available, disabled state and preserved data according to actual behavior.
Workload/service/namespace/claim views, inspect/YAML/events, logs/TTY and delete confirmations; collect errors too.

scenarios.journey: Kubernetes service access and local images
scenarios.captureRequirements: Service links/domains/Ingress/ports, namespace collisions, local-image workflow, persistent marker and unavailable service. Do not assume an Ingress controller.
Create distro/name controls, progress, shell/open/stop/restart/delete, default user and persistence. Windows equivalent uses supported user WSL integration.
Two-way host sharing, native paths, editor/terminal/SSH entry, missing path/permission error and independence from Docker engine lifecycle.
Discover actual commands, defaults/context selection, native executable invocation and credential/agent behavior; no user private keys or implicit forwarding.
Available categories, draft/validation/apply/restart, cancellation, retained values and requested versus enforced resource controls.
Quick actions/status, opt-in startup, quit versus stop, shortcuts and stale/offline presentation; record Windows adaptation separately.

scenarios.journey: Docker Desktop migration, disposable source only
scenarios.captureRequirements: Source/version selection, discovery, data selection/space estimate, progress, cancel, conflicts, verification and source retained. Conditional on source installation/license/available time. No Rancher migration assumption.
Interrupted transfer or unavailable source, safe retry and target cleanup; separate images/volumes/settings/credentials/cluster claims.
First capture scope/prompt/cancel. Execution only against an explicitly disposable reference setup after other captures and export; inspect actual retained/deleted data.
Failure versus empty inventory, log/support export, error copy/retry and useful recovery guidance; bounded disposable faults only.
Saved settings/layout/project choices, outstanding sessions/forwards, fixture data and actual engine identity after supported restart.
Dark/light, representative small/large windows, long names/large lists, focus return, keyboard navigation and permission dialogs. No pixel-equality requirement across OSes.
Entry/prompt/cancel, data retention contract and supported source/target versions. Destructive execution last, after verified export and restored remote access plan.
Not certified by cloud rental, screenshots or a remote disconnect. Needs suitable physical hardware and instrumentation; keep distinct from ordinary app restart.
